faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on my teacher salary?

bodyMarkdown:
## Introduction

If you are a teacher in Western Australia and you are paid by the hour, or you have a salary offer and want to compare it to an hourly rate, understanding how to convert between the two is essential. This guide explains the simple formula to turn your hourly rate into annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay, and covers the key Australian pay rules including the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, superannuation, and tax. We will also discuss the **teacher salary WA** context, using the latest figures from the Fair Work Commission, Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS), and Australian Taxation Office.

## The Basic Formula

The standard way to convert an hourly rate to an annual salary is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

This formula assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. For most full-time employees in Australia, the standard week is 38 hours. If you work a different number of hours, simply substitute that number.

### Example with National Minimum Wage

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour. For a 38-hour week:

- Weekly pay: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.90 (as stated by the Fair Work Commission)
- Fortnightly pay: $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80
- Annual gross annual pay: $1,004.90 × 52 = $52,254.80

If you are a casual employee, casual loading of 25% is added on top, giving $33.05 per hour, or $1,256.13 per week.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To get your fortnightly gross, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. For a teacher on an award rate of, say, $50 per hour (38 hours): weekly = $1,900, fortnightly = $3,800.

## Understanding Different Pay Rates

### Award Rates vs Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor. However, most teachers are covered by the *Teachers Award* or a state government enterprise agreement. These documents set higher minimum rates based on classification and experience. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes [pay guides](/blog) for each award. The **teacher salary WA** is not a single figure; it depends on your level and school system. The ABS reports that average full-time adult ordinary time earnings in Western Australia were $2,227.40 per week in May 2026. This is an average across all occupations, not a median for teachers. For your specific rate, refer to your award or agreement.

### Casual Loading

If you work casually, you are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate. The [timesheet tool on [the timesheet](/) you can check a checkbox to add this loading. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading; the tool adds it for you.

## Superannuation and Tax

### Super Guarantee

Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, if your annual ordinary earnings are $98,800, your employer will receive an extra $11,856 in super. This is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional contribution.

### Tax Brackets

For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here). This estimate does not include HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for a more detailed estimate.

## Using the Timesheet Tool

Our [the timesheet](/) allows you to enter your hourly rate and see the annual, weekly, and fortnightly figures. There is a checkbox to add 25% casual loading. It also estimates super and tax. Remember that the annual figure is simply hourly × hours per week × 52. For a teacher in WA, you can enter your award rate to see the conversion.

## Teacher Salary WA in Context

When searching for **teacher salary WA**, you may see averages from the ABS. The May 2026 average weekly earnings for full-time employees in WA was $2,227.40. This is not a teacher-specific median; it includes all occupations. For example, a graduate teacher might be around $80,000 per year, while a senior teacher might exceed $120,000. The formula works for any hourly rate. If your hourly rate is $60, then annual = $60 × 38 × 52 = $118,560. Fortnightly = $60 × 38 × 2 = $4,560. Super on top at 12% = $14,227.20.

## Conclusion

Converting hourly to annual pay is straightforward: multiply by hours per week and 52. Remember to use your correct award rate, not the minimum wage, unless you are a minimum wage employee. The **teacher salary WA** average is an average, not a median. Use the [reference tables](/data] for more details. Always check your pay guide and consult the Fair Work Ombudsman for award-specific rates. Use our tool to see your numbers.
